title: Spin-orbit torque-driven synthetic antiferromagnetic oscillator
authors: P. K. Rout, J. Godinho, F. Vilsmeier, R. Salikhov, J. A. Vélez, Z. Šobáň, D. Laroze, O. Gomonay, R. M. Otxoa, C. H. Back, O. Hellwig, J. Wunderlich
abstract: Antiferromagnets offer a promising route toward robust spintronic devices because of their compensated magnetic order and exchange-enhanced spin dynamics. Here, we demonstrate a spin-orbit torque (SOT)-driven antiferromagnetic oscillator based on a nanoconstriction patterned from a synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF). Spin-rectification spectroscopy reveals electrical excitation of both acoustic and optical SAF eigenmodes, whose field and frequency dependences are quantitatively described by an antiferromagnetic resonance model. In addition to these linear eigenmodes, we observe low-field spin-rectification peaks that emerge only above a threshold DC current near the spin-flop transition. Their current-polarity-dependent sign and locking to an injected RF frequency provide electrical spin-rectification signatures consistent with current-selected chiral self-oscillatory dynamics. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the threshold excitation of SOT-driven self-oscillations and injection locking, while macrospin simulations predict stable and chaotic nonlinear dynamics within the same spin-flop region. We interpret the multi-peak, weakly RF-frequency-dependent responses as a qualitative signature of complex nonlinear dynamics. These results establish SAF nanoconstrictions as an experimentally accessible platform for studying current-driven antiferromagnetic-like oscillator dynamics and motivate future work on nonlinear spintronic devices for signal processing and reservoir-computing concepts.
summary: This work investigates how spin-orbit torques drive oscillatory behavior in synthetic antiferromagnets using nanoconstrictions. By measuring the spin-rectification voltage and comparing results with simulations, the authors demonstrate electrical excitation of both linear eigenmodes and complex, current-driven self-oscillations near magnetic phase transitions. This establishes SAFs as a promising platform for nonlinear spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study demonstrates electrical excitation of spin-orbit torque (SOT)-driven antiferromagnetic oscillator dynamics using a synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) nanoconstriction.
main_result: The research establishes SAF nanoconstrictions as an accessible platform for observing complex, current-driven nonlinear dynamics, including self-oscillations and injection locking near the spin-flop transition.
method: Measurements involve spin-rectification spectroscopy (V_SRE) while applying RF currents and sweeping magnetic fields; theoretical understanding is supplemented by micromagnetic and macrospin simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a SAF multilayer stack patterned into a nanoconstriction, which exhibits distinct acoustic and optical magnetization eigenmodes. The dynamics are governed by spin-orbit torques (SOT) acting on the coupled magnetic layers.
key_observables: Spin-rectification voltage ($V_{SRE}$), resonance frequencies of acoustic/optical modes, threshold DC current for self-oscillation, and Power Spectral Density (PSD) signatures showing injection locking.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the spin-flop transition regime, critical DC currents ($J_{above}^{dc}$), and the interplay between RF excitation and bias currents.
main_assumptions: The interpretation of SOT mechanisms relies on combined evidence from mode selectivity and symmetry arguments; simulations may neglect certain damping terms for simplicity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SAF structure, selective excitation of acoustic/optical modes based on applied angle ($\Phi$), resonance frequency mapping vs. field, and PSD analysis showing transitions from linear resonance to self-oscillations under increasing DC current.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first characterizing the linear eigenmodes using SRE spectroscopy across different magnetic field angles; it then investigates nonlinear dynamics by observing threshold behavior for self-oscillations as a function of bias current, culminating in discussions on injection locking and complex chiral dynamics.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism/spintronics, the study models non-equilibrium, driven, and dissipative collective excitations (oscillators) whose dynamics are controlled by external currents, providing an experimental platform for studying nonlinear wave phenomena relevant to open quantum systems.
